key_insight: Inlet geometry strongly affects cavitation: at L/D = 5 and pressure drops above 0.2 MPa, sharp-edged inlets showed strong cavitation while chamfered inlets showed cavitation inception.
engineering_relevance: Inlet geometry and orifice length-to-diameter ratio are important design variables for managing cavitation and hydraulic flip in single-liquid injectors.
method: CFD of water flow using k–ω SST turbulence, ZGB cavitation, and VOF models.
Compared sharp-edged and chamfered inlets over pressure drops of 0.07–0.59 MPa.
Investigated orifice length-to-diameter ratios of 2, 5, and 10.
evidence_signal: Volumetric flow predictions were validated against existing experiments, and hydraulic flip at L/D = 5 and a 0.59 MPa pressure drop for the sharp-edged inlet agreed with prior experimental findings.
watch_item: The abstract reports flow-rate validation but does not quantify prediction errors or establish accuracy for local vapor distributions.
paper_title: Numerical Study of Flow and Cavitation in Single-Liquid Injectors with Sharp-Edged and Chamfered Orifice Inlets
